reconstruction.scope: Akshardham Delhi principal mandir exterior, its mapped waterside stepped platform and approach bridge, plus two mapped flanking forecourt pavilions. Nine domes, twenty quadrangled roof spires, southwest-facing open entrance porches, carved wall rhythms and an elephant plinth identify the specific temple. Distant exhibition halls, gardens, theatre and the full religious campus remain separate native structures.

reconstruction.heightBasis: The official ordinary mandir page gives141.3ft maximum height,316ft width and356ft length, nine domes and twenty quadrangled spires. The current mapped bank and approach give approximately108x95m of principal occupied platform. The main tip is modeled43m above its approach-based foundation. Dome/drum/finial allocation, porches, elephant poses, reliefs and the two forecourt pavilion roof details are photo/map-guided medium-fi estimates. Names and surveyed heights of the flanking pavilions are not established.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Original161-square/6m standard Mapzen-USGS DEM retained unchanged with198.205m raw datum. Principal foundation grade follows the formal southwest approach sample plus0.85m; each forecourt pavilion uses its own local ground sample. Only these three bounded occupied floors open ground. Opaque floor tops, deep continuous retaining faces and inward joins to the coarse boundary grade close the footprint. The source preview alone seats terrain below the occupied floors. Native water remains intact beneath and around the modeled approach bridge. Exact thresholds and canopy/building-influenced terrain levels are not surveyed.
reconstruction.elephantBasis: The official ordinary description reports148 elephants at Gajendra Pith. These148 original simplified figures supply the visible frieze rhythm; their repeated poses and approximate positions do not reproduce the individual carved narratives or claim a surveyed statue inventory.

mainStair.basis: Broad main approach stair and recessed plinth are ordinary-photo-guided estimates within the mapped waterside platform, not surveyed tread measurements.
